sections.html:
Greenwood is a city in Johnson County, about 11 miles south of downtown Indianapolis and 12 miles north of Franklin, the county seat. It sits between Interstate 65 and Interstate 69.

The city covers about 27.9 square miles, all of it land, at an elevation near 804 feet. It takes in the northern half of Pleasant Township, the northeast part of White River Township and the eastern edge of Clark Township. Greenwood has no navigable waterways, but Pleasant Run Creek crosses the northern half of the city on its roughly 5 mile path to the White River, and Grassy Creek, Tracy Ditch and Honey Creek drain other parts.

For a seller, the practical point is that Greenwood sits close to Indianapolis, which shapes commutes and what buyers expect.

sections.h2: How did Greenwood get its name and its growth?
sections.html:
The area was first home to the Delaware (Lenape) people. John B. and Isaac Smock built the first cabin in northern Johnson County in 1823, on ground that is now Greenwood Park Mall, and the settlement was first called Smocktown.

It was renamed Greenfield in 1825 and then Greenwood in 1833 to avoid confusion with another Greenfield. Greenwood was incorporated as a town in 1864 and became a fifth-class city in 1960. In 2010 the council approved moving to second-class city status.

An interurban railway, the Indianapolis, Greenwood and Franklin Railway, opened on January 1, 1900. The population grew from 49,791 in 2010 to 63,830 in the 2020 census, an increase of 28.2 percent. That pace of growth means many Greenwood houses are younger than those in older Indiana cities, though age varies by neighborhood.

Services and retail dominate. In 2023 Greenwood had 3,176 business establishments employing 25,386 people, and services made up 35.04 percent of employment, retail trade 28.46 percent and transportation and communications 9.38 percent.

  • Endress+Hauser: U.S. headquarters
  • Nachi America: machine tools
  • Amazon fulfillment center near Worthsville Road and I-65: about 1,000 employees
  • Milwaukee Electric Tool: service hub at Southtech Business Park since May 2021
  • Greenwood Park Mall: the main retail center

With retail, services and distribution all strong, a job change or a transfer is a common reason for a Greenwood owner to need a sale on a firm date.

sections.h2: What does Greenwood's climate mean for a house?
sections.html:
Greenwood has a warm temperate climate with hot summers and cold winters. The average annual temperature is 54.3 degrees, July highs average 85.2 and January lows average 22.9, and about 45 inches of precipitation falls in a year.

That swing from hot to freezing is hard on roofs, siding, driveways and air conditioning. Pleasant Run Creek runs east to west across the northern half of Greenwood, so a house in that area should check the current flood map before listing.

Roof and HVAC condition matter at any age, and a buyer who needs a lender may ask for repairs. A cash buyer looks at the same items and prices them into the offer.

sections.h2: Who handles code and permits in Greenwood?
sections.html:
The City of Greenwood has a Code Enforcement office and a Building Division, and both are at 300 S. Madison Ave. Code Enforcement (317-887-5000) inspects and reports violations, and the Building Division (317-887-5230) handles permits, inspections and unsafe structure investigations.

  • Planning handles zoning, site plan review, land alteration permits and sign permits.
  • The Advisory Plan Commission and the Board of Zoning Appeals handle zoning appeals.
  • Fire code enforcement is a separate function from building inspection.

The city's department page does not list a rental licensing office or a rental registration program, and we did not find one elsewhere. If you own a rental in Greenwood, call Code Enforcement and ask whether any registration applies before you sell.

sections.h2: What taxes and paperwork apply to a Greenwood sale?
sections.html:
Johnson County bills property tax on Greenwood houses, and Indiana sets two installments a year. The state lists the 2026 due dates as May 11 and November 10, with a 5 percent penalty within 30 days after the date and 10 percent after that. Payment goes to the county treasurer.

Indiana also uses a sales disclosure form. In the 2010 Justia copy of IC 6-1.1-5.5, the county assessor reviews the form and the auditor files it before the deed is recorded, and a recorder may not record the deed without proof the auditor received it. The state has changed parts of the process since 2010, so ask your title company for the current steps.

The residential sales disclosure chapter, IC 32-21-5, includes a section titled for presenting the disclosure form before an offer is accepted. Your agent or attorney can tell you whether it applies to your sale.

sections.h2: Which schools and roads serve Greenwood?
sections.html:
Three school corporations serve Greenwood residents: Greenwood Community School Corporation, Clark-Pleasant and Center Grove. Greenwood's own corporation includes Greenwood Community Middle School and four elementary schools: Southwest, Northeast, V.O. Isom and Westwood.

Interstate 65 has three exits on the city's east side, numbers 97, 99 and 101, and I-69 has two exits, 156 and 158, just west of the city limits. U.S. 31 and State Road 135 also run north to south through the area. Access Johnson County provides bus service, and IndyGo routes 16, 29 and 31 reach northern Greenwood.

Which school district a house falls in affects what buyers pay attention to, so confirm the address with the school corporations when you describe the property.

sections.h2: What do Greenwood sellers often face?
sections.html:
Greenwood sellers tend to deal with houses that need updating, job changes, inherited houses and rentals.

  • Aging systems: roofs, furnaces and water heaters that are near the end of their life.
  • Inherited property: heirs often live elsewhere and want to avoid managing a vacant house.
  • Rentals: tenants and lease terms affect showing schedules.
  • Timing: a job change or a move to a different part of the Indianapolis area can set a hard date.

We buy houses as-is in Greenwood. That means no repair list and no showings, so you can compare it against a listing and choose.

faqs.q: Where is Greenwood, IN, in relation to Indianapolis?
faqs.a: Greenwood is about 11 miles south of downtown Indianapolis, in Johnson County. It sits between I-65 and I-69, and the county seat, Franklin, is 12 miles to the south.

We could not confirm a rental registration program. The City of Greenwood department page lists Code Enforcement and a Building Division but no rental office. Call Code Enforcement at 317-887-5000 to check before selling a rental.

faqs.q: When are Johnson County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Indiana lists two installments a year, and the 2026 dates were May 11 and November 10. A 5 percent penalty applies within 30 days after the date, and 10 percent after that. Pay the county treasurer.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a building permit in Greenwood?
faqs.a: The Building Division at 300 S. Madison Ave., phone 317-887-5230. It handles building permits, inspections and unsafe structure investigations.

faqs.q: Which school district is my Greenwood house in?
faqs.a: Three corporations serve Greenwood residents: Greenwood Community, Clark-Pleasant and Center Grove. Your address decides which one, so confirm it with the corporations before you describe the property to a buyer.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Greenwood house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. You can list it and negotiate repairs with a financed buyer, or you can ask for a cash offer on the house as-is. Compare the net amounts and the timing.
